chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Jess Stacy as an overlooked soloist; the Trio records
summary: Freeman says Stacy had the Louis-Bix beat, was overshadowed by Teddy Wilson in Goodman's band, and played on the praised Trio records with Wettling.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now, Jess Stacy was a far more brilliant soloist than people ever realized but he was willing to just sit back, always in the background and play the accompaniment, play the band piano, never received the recognition he should have received, because he was a super soloist, having his own style.

Because Teddy Wilson, a super pianist, and a great guy, was the big thing in the Goodman band, being featured as a name and playing in the trio and quartet and what not, so Jess was always in the background, but since now we are talking about Jess, I want to say that he had a beat.
Again, that Louis-Bix beat that Lester Young had and many other great players, that very few pianists had and Jess was to influence many pianists without realizing

that he had influenced them and you must realize that after I left the Goodman band, I was with Benny a year, I did not see a great deal of Jess because he too left and went, I think, out to the Coast and then was to get out of music and work for Max Factor in the mailing room or something, I am not sure just what.
You remember he did -- he went with the Crosby band and he did do things like that.
Yes, he did. But I was not to see him because I was going off to South America and going to Europe.
You know, it's funny, when you spoke of those records, it was when you made those Trio records, that I was able to proclaim --
Yes, but we were still working.
-- you and Lester where it became were at the King (unintelligible) that there was that relation because it was right there. I think those Trio records were absolutely superb.
Well, those trio records are going to be put out here again.
They have already been put out in America, you know.
Yes, I heard. I have been over here three and a half years, as I said, but they are going to be put
out here very soon and it's all I think on the strength of Jess's playing. Of course, George Wettling played beautifully on them.
And those -- I would like to feel that those records have held up.
Oh, they have held up, they're marvelous.
